Predicted: numba fastest at every n_envs; numpy passes wforge by ~16 envs; Lua/tick RTT-bound; Lua k-ticks beats numpy only for small n; FalkorDB slowest at all n. Cheat: skipping lin_ops must fail the oracle.

controls.positive: probe_unaffordable control: affordable action moved AND paid 200/200

caveats: steps = sum of min(episode length, ticks run); np/lua/fk still pay for absorbed envs, truncated runs (lua1, fk at large n) pay less of that
fk receives the stochastic-kick schedule as an exogenous per-tick parameter (state-independent draws; client work is timed)
ref is the wforge Encounter, single thread, capped at 64 episodes

luak n=4096 P=16 FAILED: every worker raised TimeoutError reading from socket (redis-py socket_timeout None; cause not established). The first attempt hung the parent and was killed, producing no row; the rerun wrote the FAIL row
numba: 3 threads; the n=1 cells include prange dispatch overhead

hypothesis_scoring.falkordb_slowest_all_n: CONFIRMED (every cell; narrowest w0 n=4096, 40k vs lua1 43k)
hypothesis_scoring.lua1_rtt_bound_small_n: PARTLY: ~1.4-1.7 ms per call at n=1, 4-5x the 0.33 ms PING RTT; script overhead dominates
hypothesis_scoring.numpy_passes_wforge_by_16: WRONG by one octave: crossover between 16 and 64 in both worlds
hypothesis_scoring.redis_server_ceiling: aggregate ~190k steps/s across 1..16 producers; lua1 converges to it

semantic_findings: wforge stoch kick `regs[below(n)] = below(M)` evaluates RHS first: value drawn before index (all three first-draft forms had it backwards; oracle caught it)
wforge charges 0 for an unaffordable action but still applies its writes (200/200 worlds; packet PACKET_wforge_unaffordable_action.md)
FalkorDB evaluates a division inside a false CASE branch (Division by zero)

claim: B1s: the trace-hash oracle detects >=95% of episodes in which a ONE-semantic cheat's semantic was exercised (fix_unaffordable, no_regime_flip, stoch_swap in the numpy form), with 0 detections where it was not exercised; fix_unaffordable predicted weakest.

controls.cheat: three one-semantic cheats run; honest numpy form mismatches 0/960 (must be 0)
controls.negative: detections on episodes where the semantic was NOT exercised: {"fix_unaffordable": 0, "no_regime_flip": 0, "stoch_swap": 0}

science.consequence: B1's 320/320 equality proves the forms agree on EXERCISED behaviour. A form wrong only on the unaffordable-write semantic slips past ~20% of sampled episodes, so equality claims need enough episodes that the semantic is exercised AND visible
science.undetected_mechanism: not yet diagnosed (candidates: target overwritten by a lin op; landing after end)
science.verdict: the >=95% floor is KILLED by fix_unaffordable (sensitivity 0.797): an unpaid write can be absorbed without changing the trace; stoch_swap and no_regime_flip detected in every exercised episode; 0 false alarms in all three

controls.cheat: no_flee (THREATENS ignored): {"gb": "20/20 caught, 0 false alarms", "cy": "20/20 caught, 0 false alarms"}

claim: B3 op census from execution: (1) wforge Encounter.step (+ its xorshift stream) traced at bytecode level over 60 worlds executes <=8 distinct arithmetic operators and mod+mul+add are >=60% of executed arithmetic ops; (2) in the B2 graphblas form, numpy<->GraphBLAS conversion takes >50% of wall time at <=8192 entities and SuiteSparse kernel execution <30%.

controls.cheat: scope cheat RUN: an out-of-scope helper doing 50 mul + 50 mod is counted 0 when untraced (leaks: 0/5) and exactly when traced (mul 57/57, mod 50/50)
controls.positive: known op budgets counted exactly after warm-up: 4/4; cold first run in a fresh process counted 0/1000 multiplies
controls.repeatability: census over the same worlds twice in-process after a discarded warm-up: 60/60 worlds identical. A first attempt without warm-up under-counted the first traced world by ~23% in every category
controls.timing_control: outermost-call-only timing, so nested GraphBLAS calls are not double counted; group shares sum with 'unaccounted' to 1

hypothesis_scoring.b1_at_most_8_operators: WRONG: 9 semantic operators; and/xor/shifts are the xorshift stream plus Python's `& MASK64` uint64 emulation

science.instrument_finding: Python 3.12 sys.settrace opcode tracing: the first traced call in a fresh process counted 0/1000 executed multiplies; the identical call afterwards counted all of them. An earlier census without warm-up lost ~23% of world 0's ops. The mechanism inside CPython is not established
